title: A Deadline for the Cover
premise: Coral Kavanagh has spent a decade erasing problems for the Meridian Group, an embassy that exists only in encrypted filing systems, until a routine voiceprint authentication pings a server in Nairobi that shouldn't recognize her voice. The voice belongs to her, recorded years ago, in a room she has no memory of entering, and whoever controls that server begins leaking pieces of her buried past to the very people she once helped bury them for. Hunted by her own employers, shadowed by a former partner she betrayed, and blackmailed by the server's anonymous keeper, Coral must decide whether to trade the Group's founding secret, the existence of a second, sanctioned Coral Kavanagh whose crimes were pinned on her, or let the deadline pass and be erased like everyone else. In the end she burns the server, exposes the twin, and walks out of the Group's wreckage alive but officially nonexistent, finally free because no record of her remains.
about_author: Freya Marchetti is a former diplomatic translator who spent six years in postings she still cannot name, writing fiction on the flights between them. She lives in Lisbon, where she claims her neighbors know her only by a different name entirely.

chapters.title: The Quiet Line
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She cleans up a diplomat's indiscretion in Vienna with surgical calm, establishing her methods and the Meridian Group's deniable reach. A small tremor: her secure line rings with a caller ID that shouldn't exist. The emotional beat is controlled competence hiding a low hum of unease.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A routine biometric update pings: her voiceprint authenticated on a server in Nairobi, timestamped four years ago. She checks her own travel logs and finds a two-week gap she never noticed. The beat is the first crack in the wall of her own certainty.

chapters.title: The Gap
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, with a flashback fragment. She reconstructs the missing fortnight through receipts and muscle memory, finding a hotel keycard and a scar she can't explain. Her handler, Voss, deflects her questions too smoothly. The beat is dread dressed as diligence.

chapters.title: Nairobi Calling
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She flies to Kenya off-book. The server sits in a co-location facility rented by a shell company whose signature she recognizes: her own handwriting. An anonymous message offers a meeting. The beat is hunter becoming quarry.

chapters.title: The Man Who Kept Her Voice
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Coral and a new figure, Odhiambo, a disgraced archivist. He reveals he holds recordings of Coral committing acts she has no memory of, and that someone sold them to him. The beat is vertigo: evidence that contradicts the self.

chapters.title: What the Recordings Show
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Watching herself on camera, she notices details that don't fit: a mole she doesn't have, a left-handed signature, a slightly different voice. Someone was wearing her identity. The beat shifts from guilt to cold, clarifying anger.

chapters.title: The Other Kavanagh
chapters.summary: Coral's POV with Voss interlude. She learns of the Meridian Group's 'mirror program': sanctioned operatives given agents' identities to absorb their crimes. Voss warns her to come home. The beat is betrayal by the institution that made her.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Priced
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Her former partner Elias Reyes resurfaces, sent to retrieve her, and she must decide whether he's protection or executioner. They share a tense, honest night in a safehouse. The beat is loyalty tested against truth.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Odhiambo's POV. He sets the terms: the Group's founding secret in exchange for the recordings, seventy-two hours, or everything goes to the people Coral once destroyed. The beat is a clock starting, pressure becoming physical.

chapters.title: The Founding Secret
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Digging into the mirror program's origins, she finds the Group was built on a sanctioned massacre blamed on a dead operative, Coral's predecessor, whose file carries her own face. The beat is horror recast as inheritance.

chapters.title: Elias's Choice
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Ordered to kill her, he instead burns his own cover to buy her time, and confesses he helped design the mirror program years ago. The beat is guilt, sacrifice, and a friendship broken and remade.

chapters.title: Voss's Offer
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Voss offers her a new identity, a clean slate, if she lets Odhiambo die and the secret stay buried. For one chapter, Coral genuinely considers it. The beat is temptation: the comfort of forgetting.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, ticking-clock structure in short scenes. She races across three cities assembling proof of the twin operative, 'Kavanagh-2', while Group hunters close in. The beat is momentum, exhaustion, resolve hardening into steel.

chapters.title: The Mirror
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She finally meets her double, Dana Voss, the director's daughter, who wears Coral's face-prints and shows no remorse. Their conversation is the thematic heart: which of them is real? The beat is recognition and revulsion.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Archive
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Coral and Odhiambo. The Group hits Odhiambo's archive; he dies protecting the recordings, passing Coral the decryption key. The beat is grief converted into obligation, the cost made flesh.

chapters.title: Everything Attributable
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She leaks the mirror program to three journalists simultaneously, making suppression impossible, and watches the Group's deniability collapse in real time. The beat is catharsis with a shadow: she's now the most hunted woman in Europe.

chapters.title: The Director's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, confronting Director Voss in his burning office. He argues the mirror program saved thousands; she refuses the arithmetic. Elias arrives to hold the door. The beat is justice outside the law, chosen deliberately.

chapters.title: Dana's Last Authentication
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Dana, exposed and disowned, tries to kill Coral and assume her life entirely; their fight is mirrored, brutal, intimate. Coral wins by knowing herself, finally, better than her double does. The beat is identity won in blood.

chapters.title: Erasure
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, quiet and procedural. She uses the Group's own tools to delete every record of Coral Kavanagh, including her own, leaving Dana's crimes orphaned and unattributable. The beat is strange peace in self-annihilation.

chapters.title: The Woman Without a File
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Weeks later, in Lisbon, a woman with no passport and no past orders coffee, watches the news coverage of the collapsed Group, and feels the deadline pass without her. The beat is freedom that tastes like ash and light.

chapters.title: A Voice in the Crowd
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He finds her, as promised, carrying the only copy of Odhiambo's archive, and asks what she'll do with a truth no one can attach her name to. The beat is loyalty renewed on honest terms.

chapters.title: Deadline Met
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, closing. She mails the archive's key to a journalist, keeps nothing, and walks into a city that will never know her name, finally the author of her own record. The beat is resolution: invisible by choice, at last.
